data: In the leftmost plot, is the highest identification rate reached by the black line when alpha is 0.6?

The question asks whether the highest identification rate reached by the black line occurs at an alpha value of 0.6 in the leftmost plot. 

From the caption, we know that the figure shows the evolution of the identification rate as a function of alpha and beta, combining the first and second eigenresiduals according to Equations (5) and (6). The leftmost plot represents the relationship between the identification rate and alpha.

Looking at the leftmost plot, the black line represents the identification rate as a function of alpha. Observing the curve, the highest point appears to be slightly above 80% and is reached around alpha = 0.8, not at alpha = 0.6. Therefore, the highest identification rate is not reached at alpha = 0.6 but rather at a higher value of alpha.
